title: Commodification

draft.title: Commodification
card: Commodification is the process of turning culture into products that can be bought and sold. Things that were once shared, made or enjoyed freely can become goods with a price.
Common examples are band merchandise, concert tickets, branded sports jerseys and streaming subscriptions. Each one puts a price on a way of taking part in popular culture.
A fan who buys a team scarf is paying to show belonging. A company that sells it earns money from that wish to belong.
Commodification can make culture easy to reach and pay creators. It can also mean that taking part depends on being able to pay.
draft.remember: Commodification is culture turned into a product with a price.

a.q: Which is an example of commodification?
opts: A film studio sells scarves printed with its film's logo
Friends sing together at a school music night
A fan writes a review and shares it with classmates
A council holds a free outdoor concert in a park
a.why: Printing a film's logo on scarves turns the film's culture into a product sold for money. The free concert is not commodified, because no price is put on taking part.
a.clue: Look for culture that has been given a price.

b.q: A band in Newcastle starts selling signed shirts and a monthly paid fan club. Which statement best describes what has happened?
opts: The band's culture is being turned into products to sell
The band's music has become less popular with its fans
The band's fans have stopped expressing who they are
The band's music is now spreading to other countries
b.why: Shirts and a paid fan club are products that put a price on the band's culture, so this is commodification. It does not show the band is less popular, and nothing in the case says it is spreading overseas.
b.clue: Focus on what is now being sold, not on who is listening.

a.best: A film studio sells scarves printed with its film's logo

b.best: The band's culture is being turned into products to sell
